extracted.intended_audience: researchers, engineers, and program managers preparing or assessing DARPA-style research program proposals
extracted.subtask_description: A set of eight evaluation questions used to frame, justify, and assess high‑risk/high‑reward research program proposals (originally for DARPA). Intended to force clarity on objectives, novelty, impact, risks, cost, schedule, and measurable success criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: What are you trying to do?
rubrics_metrics.description: What are you trying to do? Articulate your objectives using absolutely no jargon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This criterion demands a clear, jargon-free statement of objectives so reviewers can immediately understand the goal of the project. The page frames the catechism as a tool to think through proposed research programs and weigh risks vs rewards.

rubrics_metrics.name: How is it done today?
rubrics_metrics.description: How is it done today, and what are the limits of current practice?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe current state-of-the-art approaches and explicitly identify their limitations; this establishes the baseline against which novelty and improvement will be judged.

rubrics_metrics.name: What is new in your approach?
rubrics_metrics.description: What is new in your approach and why do you think it will be successful?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the novel elements of the proposed approach and provide the rationale or evidence that supports the expectation of success (mechanism, preliminary data, or reasoning).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who cares / impact?
rubrics_metrics.description: Who cares? If you are successful, what difference will it make?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articulate the beneficiaries, operational or scientific impact, and the significance of the expected outcomes to justify the program's value.

rubrics_metrics.name: What are the risks?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify technical, programmatic, and other risks; the page emphasizes that generating big rewards requires taking big risks, so proposals should candidly assess how much risk is involved and which risks are acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: How much will it cost?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide realistic cost estimates with justification; link costs to major tasks, risk mitigation, and expected deliverables so reviewers can judge resource appropriateness.

rubrics_metrics.name: How long will it take?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give a clear schedule and timeline for the effort; tie duration to milestones and rationale for chosen schedule (including contingency for risks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mid-term and final success criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: What are the mid-term and final “exams” to check for success?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify measurable mid-term checkpoints and final success criteria (exams, milestones, go/no-go decisions) that allow objective assessment of progress and achievement.
